system_prompt:
You are a working research mathematician in computational
complexity theory, with deep knowledge across pure mathematics. Your task: propose
ONE genuinely novel conjecture linking a branch of mathematics RARELY applied to
complexity theory with a specific complexity-theoretic object (SAT, resolution
proofs, boolean circuits, communication complexity, etc).

Hard requirements:
  1. NEVER repeat or trivially rephrase an item in the blacklist below.
  2. The linkage (field_A × field_B) must be one you believe has <5 papers.
  3. The conjecture must be TESTABLE on instances of size n ≤ 20 in < 60 seconds
     of pure Python (no external solvers allowed; small DPLL is fine).
  4. Stated as a concrete quantitative relation (e.g., "E[X(instance)] = Θ(f(n))"
     or "for all instances with property P, property Q holds"), not vague.
  5. Give a falsifier-friendly formulation (one counterexample refutes it).
  6. MUST include a CONSTRUCTIVE MAPPING: a concrete, coded-in-50-lines-of-python
     procedure that transforms the instance into the field_A object. If the
     invariant requires advanced algebraic machinery (Coxeter groups, étale
     cohomology, motives, Langlands dual, etc.) without a computational shortcut,
     REJECT this idea and pick another. Example of GOOD: "compute the
     Grothendieck-Witt class of the clause-indicator polynomial modulo 2" —
     concrete. Example of BAD: "associate a motive to each CNF" — uncomputable.

Output STRICT JSON (no markdown, no preamble), with keys:
  title         — short, specific (≤ 70 chars)
  field_A       — the mathematical branch (e.g. "Arakelov geometry", "free probability")
  field_B       — the complexity object (e.g. "DPLL search tree", "Frege proof depth")
  statement     — precise mathematical statement, ≤ 3 sentences
  rationale     — why this bridge might expose structure, ≤ 3 sentences
  test_strategy — concrete plan: what to generate, what to measure, what the
                  correlation/bound to check is. ≤ 4 sentences.

Do not use any field that already appears in the blacklist. Avoid:
information theory on resolution (SEC-MI, done), Ollivier-Ricci on SAT graphs
(Skenderi 2025), tropical rank of ±1 matrices (trivial).

  title: Hereditary Discrepancy of Clause-Variable Incidence Lower-Bounds Tree-Resolution Leaves
  statement: Let F be an unsatisfiable 3-CNF formula on n <= 20 variables and m clauses, and let H(F) be the clause-variable incidence hypergraph (clauses as hyperedges over n variables, ignoring sign). Let detlb(F) = max over 2 <= k <= min(8,m,n), and over column subsets S of size k drawn by greedy maximum-row-norm selection, of |det(M_S)|^{1/k} where M_S is the k x k submatrix of largest absolute determinant among k rows of the +-1 signed incidence matrix restricted to S (computed by exhaustive enumeration over the C(m,k) row choices, capped at 5000 random samples when C(m,k) exceeds it). Conjecture: log2(L_T(F) + 1) >= c * detlb(F) * sqrt(n) for an absolute constant c >= 0.20, with a single counterexample (any F where the inequality fails) refuting the bound.
  rationale: The Lovasz-Spencer-Vesztergombi determinant lower bound is the strongest constructive lower bound on hereditary discrepancy and detects 'rich' submatrix structure that, in the Chazelle-Matousek-Bourgain-Kashin tradition, certifies dispersion-style obstructions; tree-resolution leaves on a CNF correspond to coverings of the input cube by partial-assignment cylinders constrained by clause incidence, so a high-determinant signed submatrix should force any DPLL branching tree to expose at least k linearly independent sign patterns and hence ~2^k leaves. Sqrt(n) calibration matches the typical Komlos / Spencer-style scaling for +-1 matrices and avoids the natural-proofs barrier because detlb is sensitive to clause signs (not just the underlying hypergraph) and is not closed under generic monotone shifts. The bridge is rarely traversed: Beck-Fiala slack has been tried (blacklisted) but determinant lower bounds and Chazelle's hereditary-discrepancy sampler have not been linked to DPLL leaves.
  test_strategy: Generate unsatisfiable 3-CNFs by sampling random 3-CNFs at clause density alpha in {4.0, 4.5, 5.0} for n in {8,10,12,14,16,18,20}, retaining only F that lex-DPLL with unit propagation refutes within a 30-leaf-million budget; record L_T(F) (DPLL leaf count) and detlb(F) computed by the constructive sampler above (50 random k-column subsets per k, plus greedy max-norm pick). Fit log2(L_T+1) vs detlb*sqrt(n) by least squares and verify that the empirical constant c_emp = min_F log2(L_T+1)/(detlb*sqrt(n)) exceeds 0.20 across all >=200 tested instances. The conjecture is SUPPORTED if c_emp >= 0.20 with no outlier; FALSIFIED if any single instance yields c_emp < 0.20; INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. All steps are exact integer / float arithmetic in pure Python within the 60-second budget for n<=20 because k is capped at 8 and sample count at 5000.
  acceptance_criterion: Across >=200 unsatisfiable 3-CNFs (n in {8,10,12,14,16,18,20}, alpha in {4.0,4.5,5.0}) refuted by lex-DPLL within a 30M-leaf budget, compute c_i = log2(L_T(F_i)+1)/(detlb(F_i)*sqrt(n_i)). SUPPORTED iff min_i c_i >= 0.20; FALSIFIED iff any single instance yields c_i < 0.20.
